## Introduction

Point maps show where things are: case residences, laboratories, care homes, or
the centre of each reporting area. The `point_map()` function plots points from
latitude and longitude columns in a data frame. Points can be coloured by a
category or a value and sized by a numeric variable to make a bubble map.

Like other epiviz functions, `point_map()` has a static ggplot output, but
returns an interactive leaflet map by default (set `dynamic = FALSE` for the
static output). Both static and dynamic maps show an OpenStreetMap basemap by
default. The interactive map also supports switching between basemaps,
clustering, click popups, hover labels and a measuring tool.

## Prerequisites

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  eval = TRUE,
  fig.width = 8,
  fig.height = 6,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE
)
```

```{r load-libraries}
library(epiviz)
library(dplyr)
library(sf)
```

### Prepare the data

The `PHEC_boundaries_2016` dataset includes a `lat` and `long` column for the
centre of each region. This example joins regional detection counts from
`lab_data` onto those centres.

```{r prepare-data}
region_detections <- lab_data |>
  filter(!is.na(region)) |>
  group_by(region) |>
  summarise(detections = n()) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(detection_level = ifelse(detections > median(detections), "High", "Low"))

region_points <- PHEC_boundaries_2016 |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  inner_join(region_detections, by = c("phec16nm" = "region")) |>
  mutate(popup_html = paste0("<strong>", phec16nm, "</strong><br>Detections: ", detections))
```

## Example 1: Static bubble map

Supply the name of a numeric column as `point_size` to scale each point by its
value. `point_size_range` sets the smallest and largest point sizes. Add
boundaries for context with `border_shape_name`. Static maps draw the first
provider in `basemaps` as background tiles, so they need an internet connection.
Use `basemaps = NULL` for a map without tiles.

```{r static-bubble-map, fig.cap="Detections by region, sized and coloured by count.", fig.alt="Static map of England on a topographic background with a circle at each region centre, sized and coloured by number of detections."}
point_map(
  dynamic = FALSE,
  params = list(
    df = region_points,
    lat = "lat",
    long = "long",
    colour_var = "detections",
    point_colours = "YlOrRd",
    point_size = "detections",
    point_size_range = c(6, 20),
    size_legend_title = "Detections",
    legend_title = "Detections",
    map_title = "Detections by region",
    map_footer = "Source: epiviz lab_data",
    basemaps = "Esri.WorldTopoMap",
    border_shape_name = UK_boundaries_2023,
    border_code_col = "CTRY23NM",
    border_areaname = "England"
  )
)
```

## Example 2: Interactive categorical map

For a categorical `colour_var`, supply a named vector of `point_colours` to set
the colour of each group. Dynamic maps (the default) support `click_popups_col`,
which names a column of html shown when a point is clicked, and `point_labels`,
which names a column shown on hover. Supplying more than one basemap adds a
layer control.

```{r interactive-map, fig.cap="Interactive map of regions coloured by detection level.", fig.alt="Interactive map with a circle at each region centre coloured by high or low detection level."}
point_map(
  params = list(
    df = region_points,
    lat = "lat",
    long = "long",
    colour_var = "detection_level",
    point_colours = c("High" = "#8A1B61", "Low" = "#007C91"),
    point_size = 10,
    point_border_colour = "white",
    click_popups_col = "popup_html",
    point_labels = "phec16nm",
    basemaps = c("Uncluttered" = "Esri.WorldGrayCanvas", "Detailed" = "OpenStreetMap"),
    legend_title = "Detection level",
    map_title = "Detection level by region",
    measure_tool = TRUE
  )
)
```

## Example 3: Interactive clustered case map

For case-level data, `cluster = TRUE` groups nearby points into clusters that
split apart as you zoom in. Each case below is placed at a random position
around its region's centre.

```{r clustered-map, fig.cap="Interactive clustered map of individual detections.", fig.alt="Interactive map of individual detections grouped into numbered clusters."}
set.seed(1)

case_points <- lab_data |>
  filter(!is.na(region)) |>
  inner_join(st_drop_geometry(PHEC_boundaries_2016), by = c("region" = "phec16nm")) |>
  mutate(
    lat = lat + rnorm(n(), sd = 0.2),
    long = long + rnorm(n(), sd = 0.3)
  )

point_map(
  params = list(
    df = case_points,
    lat = "lat",
    long = "long",
    colour_var = "organism_species_name",
    point_colours = c("#007C91", "#8A1B61", "#FF7F32"),
    cluster = TRUE,
    legend_title = "Organism species",
    legend_pos = "bottomright",
    map_zoom = data.frame(LONG = -2.5, LAT = 53.5, zoom = 6)
  )
)
```

## Static and dynamic differences

| Feature | Static (`dynamic = FALSE`) | Dynamic (`dynamic = TRUE`, the default) |
|---|---|---|
| Colour and size by variable | Yes | Yes |
| Boundary overlay (`border_shape_name`) | Yes | Yes |
| Basemap tiles (`basemaps`) | First basemap only | Yes, with a layer control for several |
| Clustering, popups, hover labels | No | Yes |
| Measuring tool | No | Yes |
| Size legend | Added automatically when sizing by a variable | Custom legend via `size_legend` |

If you supply a dynamic-only parameter when `dynamic = FALSE`, `point_map()`
warns that it will be ignored.

## Data checks

`point_map()` removes rows with a missing `lat` or `long` and warns you how many
it removed. Points with a missing value in the `point_size` column are drawn at
the smallest size in `point_size_range`, also with a warning.
